first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and memory_31 and memory_86 both show that simplification and shortening onboarding drive durable activation lift. I'm verifying memory_31 (signup simplification) and memory_73 (promotional pricing) to confirm effect sizes and scope. Memory_73 is critical to verify because competitor pricing pressure on SMBs might make promotional pricing the better move, but the activation decline suggests onboarding friction is the more immediate lever. If memory_31's effect is robust and generalizable, simplify_onboarding addresses both the activation and completion declines and has lower downstream brand/margin risk than pricing action. This preserves the option to run a promotional pricing test if simplification underperforms. Standard experiment scale lets us measure real impact without over-committing before we understand the quality/retention interaction.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirmed the critical distinction: memory_31 (signup simplification) shows durable +4% qualified revenue with only -1% retention risk on SMB, while memory_73 (promotional pricing) drives short-term signup spike (+31%) but catastrophic renewal failure (-12% 30-day retention). Given the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue and the current activation/completion decline, simplify_onboarding is the only defensible choice. Competitor pricing pressure is real, but memory_73's data proves discounting acquired accounts we cannot retain is value-destructive. Onboarding simplification addresses both the 6% activation and 4% completion declines, works on the SMB segment being attacked, and carries measurable retention safety. Standard experiment scale allows measurement before broader rollout, preserving option value if results diverge from memory_31 or if competitor dynamics shift.
